To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction between 2C ATPase and the capsid protein VP1 is required to rescue the encapsidation of a quasi-infective chimaera consisting of the non- structural proteins of PV and the capsid precursor protein of CAV20.

(i) the non-structural proteins of poliovirus are sufficient to direct the encapsidation of a heterologous capsid protein and (ii) a direct interaction between non-structural and capsid proteins is required for enterovirus morphogenesis.

(i) a direct interaction between the viral proteins 2CATP and VP3 is required for enterovirus morphogenesis, and (ii) this interaction is specific, i.e., the 2CATP-VP3 interaction must be formed between the cognate proteins of the same virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of RNA virus morphogenesis.
the mechanism of enteroviral morphogenesis.
the first identification of a protein-protein interaction required for the formation of enteroviral particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of enterovirus morphogenesis is based on a direct protein-protein interaction between the nonstructural protein 2C ATPase and the capsid protein VP 3.
morphogenesis of PV-like viruses is driven by protein-protein interaction between 2CTPase and the capsid protein VP1/VP3.
the mechanism of enterovirus morphogenesis is based on the direct interaction between 1) the 2CATPases of the replication complex and 2) the capsid protein(s) of the nascent virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specificity of morphogenesis is explained by a direct interaction between two viral proteins, 2CATP and VP3, which are translated in the same cell.
the specificity of morphogenesis of enteroviruses is determined by the interaction between the 2CATPases and capsid proteins.
morphogenesis is a consequence of the interaction of two viral proteins, the nonstructural protein 2CA and the capsid protein VP0/3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a direct interaction between two viral proteins, 2CATP and VP3, is required for enterovirus morphogenesis.
the mechanism of morphogeneses is not universal but depends on the virus and the cellular environment.
a protein-protein interaction between 2C and VP3 is sufficient for PV morphogenesis, and that the specificity of the interaction explains the observed encapsidation specificity.
